# Maho

> Maho is a free, open source (OSL-3.0) ecommerce platform that you host and own. It is fully featured out of the box: a page builder, eleven industry themes, one-step checkout, email automation, customer segments, gift cards, product feeds, passkeys and an accessibility scanner are in the core, where other platforms sell them as paid add-ons. It is ready for AI, with an AI assistant in the admin, an MCP server for AI agents and a storefront that agents can read. It runs on a modern stack: PHP 8.5, Symfony, Doctrine DBAL, Tailwind CSS 4 and vanilla JavaScript.

Maho grew from Magento 1 and OpenMage. It keeps the architecture that made Magento 1 a great platform to build on (modules, events, layouts, the EAV catalog, multi-store), and the Maho team rebuilt everything around it: the admin, the storefront, the checkout, the APIs, the database layer and the toolchain.

## Facts

- Started in July 2024. First release: 24.9.0 (September 2024). Latest release: 26.11.0 (November 2026).
- A new release every two months, with calendar versions (YY.M), plus bugfix and security patch releases (YY.M.1, YY.M.2, ...) for the current release. The team supports the latest release, because it believes that regular upgrades keep a store secure and free of technical debt. The release notes list every change that needs an action.
- Requirements of 26.11: PHP 8.5 or 8.6; MySQL 8.4+, MariaDB 10.11+, PostgreSQL 15+ (beta) or SQLite (beta); Apache, Nginx, Caddy or FrankenPHP.
- No license fee and no revenue share. The code is on GitHub under OSL-3.0.
- Maintained by Fabrizio Balliano, a former OpenMage maintainer, with community contributors. Funded by sponsors, by the NLnet NGI TALER Fund (European Commission, Next Generation Internet), by Maho Cloud, the official managed hosting, and by Maho Admin, the official mobile app.
- Maho merges the fixes and security patches of OpenMage. It removed Zend Framework 1, Varien, PrototypeJS and ExtJS. The `maho` CLI has commands that move Magento 1 code (routes, observers, cron jobs) to the new structure.

## Features in the core

- Commerce: multi-website and multi-store, multiple currencies and languages, simple, configurable, bundle, grouped, downloadable and virtual products, customer groups, tier prices, catalog and cart price rules, product relationship rules, dynamic categories, custom lines in admin orders.
- Checkout and payments: one-step checkout, guest checkout, real-time EU VAT number validation (VIES), PayPal on the v6 SDK (buttons, card fields, saved payment methods), and official modules for Mollie, Revolut, Braintree, Przelewy24 and GNU Taler on the marketplace.
- Shipping: UPS, FedEx and USPS on their REST APIs, and a bridge to external shipping rate APIs.
- Storefront: eleven industry themes on Tailwind CSS 4 and daisyUI 5, a live theme editor, a page builder for CMS pages, CMS blocks and blog posts, product page gallery layouts, a blog with categories, layered navigation with multi-select filters.
- Marketing: customer segments, email automation, gift cards, product feeds for Google (including local inventory), Meta, Bing, Pinterest, OpenAI, Idealo and Trovaprezzi, newsletters, Bestsellers and On Sale widgets.
- SEO: Schema.org structured data (JSON-LD), hreflang tags, SEO-friendly layered navigation, a robots.txt generator per store view, 410 Gone for deleted products.
- AI: an AI assistant on every admin page that reads the user guide and runs scheduled tasks; an AI module for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, OpenRouter, Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible host; a store MCP server with OAuth 2.1 login; storefront pages in markdown for AI agents; `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` for each store; robots.txt rules for AI crawlers.
- Customers and security: passkeys, two-factor authentication for customers and admins, magic link login, social login with Google, Apple and Facebook, a self-hosted CAPTCHA, rate limiting and honeypots on public forms, an admin activity log, encryption key rotation.
- Compliance: a WCAG accessibility scanner for the European Accessibility Act, the EU revocation button, PDF invoices, shipments and credit memos attached to emails, an email log.
- Admin: a redesigned admin with light and dark mode, an image editor with local AI background removal, content versioning, a health check page, cron management, background exports and imports, and Maho Admin, the official mobile app for Android (iOS coming soon).
- APIs: a REST and GraphQL API (beta) with JWT authentication, granular permissions and an OpenAPI 3.1 spec, plus the legacy REST and SOAP APIs of Magento 1.
- Performance and operations: a full reindex three to five times faster than before, deferred image thumbnails, speculation rules for instant page loads, Redis, an async job queue on Symfony Messenger, OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs, media and files on S3, Google Cloud Storage or Azure.
- Developer tools: the `maho` CLI (install, import, reindex, `db:export` and `db:import`), official Docker images on FrankenPHP, a DDEV project type, a Composer plugin, a PHPStan plugin, editor plugins for PhpStorm, VS Code and Zed with a language server and an MCP server for the codebase, a declarative database schema, observers, cron jobs and routes as PHP attributes.
- Languages: official language packs for 13 languages.
- Supply chain: CycloneDX SBOMs with daily vulnerability scans, and SLSA Build Level 3 provenance for releases.

## Who Maho fits

- Magento 1 and OpenMage stores that want a modern, maintained platform without a rewrite. The architecture is the same, so the migration costs much less than a move to another platform.
- Small and medium stores, and the agencies that build them, that want to own their code, their data and their server, with no fees on their revenue.
- Stores that sell in several countries, languages and currencies from one installation.
- European stores: hosted in any country they pick, with the EU revocation button, EU VAT validation and an accessibility scanner for the European Accessibility Act.
- Stores that want AI in their daily work, with the provider they pick, including a local model.
- PHP developers who know Magento 1 or Symfony.

- [Getting started](https://mahocommerce.com/about/getting-started/): requirements and installation with Composer, Docker or DDEV
- [Migrate to Maho](https://mahocommerce.com/about/migrate-to-maho/): move a Magento 1 or OpenMage store to Maho
- [Origins and differences](https://mahocommerce.com/about/origins/): what Maho kept from Magento 1 and what changed
- [Release strategy](https://mahocommerce.com/about/release-strategy/): versions, support policy and the reasons for it
- [Security and supply chain](https://mahocommerce.com/about/security/): SBOMs, vulnerability scans, SLSA provenance, how to report a vulnerability
- [User guide](https://mahocommerce.com/user-guide/): the features of the admin, for store owners
- [Developer guide](https://mahocommerce.com/developer/guide/introduction/): modules, config, layouts, ORM
- [REST and GraphQL API](https://mahocommerce.com/api/v2/): the API, its authentication and conventions
- [MCP server](https://mahocommerce.com/api/v2/mcp/): connect an AI agent to a store
- [Hosting](https://mahocommerce.com/hosting/web-server/): web server, Redis, storage, cron, FrankenPHP
